Senses.Explanation: No-thought is defined as functioning amid thought without fixation, not forcibly blanking the mind. Huineng places it beside no-form and no-abiding and defines it as being amid thought without thought. He says seeing all things without the mind becoming stained is no-thought, while thinking of nothing and cutting thought off is bondage and a one-sided view. He also warns that eliminating a single thought is death. The Dunhuang recension independently defines no-thought as seeing all things while sticking to none. Huineng's character-by-character explanation says what is absent is dual marks and the dust-and-toil mind, while what is thought of is true-thus original nature. Shenhui answers that the no-thought teaching is asserted as neither existent nor nonexistent. Nanyue Jiqi quotes a threefold formula linking realization of no-thought with penetrating things and seeing the awakened ones' realm. These are explicit textual boundaries against a blank-mind gloss.
Senses.Note: Exact frozen-corpus count: 934 hits in 166 files and 163 works. Seven witnesses across five works meet the packet floor and cover axiom, definition, rejection of blankness, independent recension, character explanation, existence question, and later public deployment.

Occurrences.Kwic: 善知識！我此法門，從上以來，先立無念為宗，無相為體，無住為本。無相者，於相而離相。無念者，於念而無念。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch (六祖大師法寶壇經): Huineng establishes no-thought as the axiom and defines it as being amid thought without thought.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若得解脫，即是般若三昧，即是無念。何名無念？若見一切法，心不染著，是為無念。用即遍一切處，亦不著一切處。但淨本心，使六識出六門，於六塵中無染無雜，來去自由，通用無滯，即是般若三昧、自在解脫，名無念行。若百物不思，當令念絕，即是法縛，即名邊見。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch (六祖大師法寶壇經): Huineng defines no-thought as seeing without attachment and rejects thinking of nothing as bondage.

Occurrences.Kwic: 善知識！於諸境上，心不染，曰無念。於自念上，常離諸境，不於境上生心。若只百物不思，念盡除却，一念絕即死，別處受生，是為大錯。學道者思之。若不識法意，自錯猶可，更誤他人；自迷不見，又謗佛經，所以立無念為宗。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch (六祖大師法寶壇經): Huineng says no-thought is unstained mind amid objects and warns that eliminating a single thought is death.

Occurrences.Kwic: 悟般若三昧，即是無念。何名無念？無念法者，見一切法，不著一切法；遍一切處，不著一切處。常淨自性，使六賊從六門走出，於六塵中不離不染，來去自由，即是般若三昧，自在解脫，名無念行。莫百物不思，當令念絕，即是法縛，即名邊見。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dunhuang Platform Sutra (南宗頓教最上大乘摩訶般若波羅蜜經六祖惠能大師於韶州大梵寺施法壇經): Huineng defines no-thought as seeing all things without sticking to any and rejects cutting thought off.

Occurrences.Kwic: 善知識！云何立無念為宗？只緣口說見性，迷人於境上有念，念上便起邪見，一切塵勞妄想從此而生。自性本無一法可得，若有所得，妄說禍福，即是塵勞邪見，故此法門立無念為宗。善知識！無者無何事？念者念何物？無者無二相，無諸塵勞之心。念者念真如本性。真如即是念之體，念即是真如之用。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch (六祖大師法寶壇經): Huineng explains that absence concerns dual marks and defilement while thought concerns true-thus original nature.

Senses.Explanation: In these passages Wunian is the style name of the Ming master Shenyou rather than the no-thought term. His collection's title names Chan Master Huangbo Wunian, and a biographical statement gives his personal name Shenyou and style Wunian. A later record quotes Tao Shikui naming Master Wunian during a fireside exchange, and separately quotes Zhanran Yuancheng visiting and questioning him. Personal-name, title, and dialogue syntax force a proper-name sense.
Senses.Note: Four explicit witnesses across two works establish the proper-name referent.
